battle.name: 武陟之戰
battle.brief: 北周大象二年（五八〇年）秋，尉遲迥之亂的兵鋒西進至河內郡武陟，隔黃河與洛陽對峙；郡兵與關隴援軍在此接戰，保住了通往洛陽與關中的津渡。卡面的斯巴達長矛是希臘方陣的重步兵兵器，本役並未使用，只作對照——北周步卒同樣以長柄矛槊結陣前推，靠隊形、旗鼓與弓弩壓制，而非單兵格鬥。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 北周大象二年（五八〇年）秋，周宣帝宇文贊崩，幼帝宇文閔即位，隨王楊堅以相國總百揆掌禁軍宿衛，丞相尉遲迥自鄴城舉兵反之。交戰的兩方是關隴軍功世族與河北軍功舊臣兩個集團：楊堅一方以八柱國、十二大將的家將部曲為骨幹，輔以洛陽周圍的州郡兵、宿衛禁軍與河內郡的郡兵，號令由洛陽中樞發出，糧秣沿黃河與洛陽—武陟—太行陘道這一線輸送；尉遲迥一方以相州治鄴城為巢，據相、冀、兗、曹、鄆諸州，徵集河北鄉兵與北周宿衛舊部，眾號十餘萬，郡縣多望風歸附。尉遲迥的部署以鄴城為根本，另分兵沿黃河往東郡白馬津與西面的武陟推進，企圖先取太行孔道上的津渡，把洛陽與河北、與關中的往來切斷。雙方都自稱奉周室、護幼主，實際爭的是北周的相權與兵權歸屬；武陟之戰就是這條補給線上的一場遭遇。
countriesEn: In the autumn of the second year of the Daxiang era (580) of Northern Zhou, Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun died, the child-emperor Yuwen Min was enthroned, and Yang Jian, Prince of Sui, as chancellor and general administrator of all affairs took charge of the palace guards, while Chancellor Yuwen Jiong raised his standard at Ye city in rebellion. The two sides were the Guanlong military-aristocratic group and the Hebei military establishment. Yang Jian's side was built on the family troops and retainers of the Eight Pillars and the Twelve Generals, supplemented by the provincial levies of the districts around Luoyang, the imperial guard, and the county troops of Henei Commandery; its orders came out of the Luoyang centre, and its grain and provisions moved along the Yellow River and the line of road running Luoyang, Wuzhi and the Taihang passes. Yuwen Jiong's side used the provincial capital of Xiangzhou, Ye city, as its nest, held Xiang, Ji, Yan, Cao and Yun prefectures, mustered Hebei village levies and former Northern Zhou guard troops, and claimed a force of more than a hundred thousand, with commanderies and counties throughout the region submitting in its wake. His scheme was to root himself at Ye while dispatching columns along the Yellow River towards Baima Ford in Dong Commandery and towards Wuzhi to the west, in order to seize first the fords on the road through the Taihang range and sever the links of Luoyang with Hebei and with Guanzhong. Both sides professed to serve the Zhou house and to protect the child-emperor; what was really at stake was the custody of the chancellor's authority and of Northern Zhou's military command. The battle of Wuzhi was an encounter on that line of supply.
people: 尉遲迥是宇文泰的舊將，西魏八柱國之一，歷事周武帝與周宣帝，官至丞相、大冢宰，是北周晚期真正能壓住外戚與軍方的重臣；他在河北經營數代，趙郡、魏郡的舊族與北周宿衛都認他這面旗，鄴城一帶的城防與糧秣也由他一手安排。楊堅是關隴集團的核心，宇文泰的外孫，父楊忠亦為八柱國之一；宣帝崩後，他以隨王兼相國總百揆，握禁軍宿衛與詔令，最終在開皇元年正月受周恭帝禪讓。楊堅在西線最倚重都督王誼，太原人，與楊堅自少年即為摯交，被任為行軍元帥統五州兵，是清漳破敵、進逼鄴城的主帥；並州總管韋俊、陝州總管韋雲起各領騎兵與步卒參戰，韋俊初戰失利退兵。與武陟同在黃河一線的東郡，郡守于仲文率六十餘騎拒敵，斬首五百餘級，其後突圍西退；河內郡一線的守將姓名未見於現存記載，只知郡兵在武陟據城拒守、待援。尉遲迥一方另有劉辟疆、師大俠、段任領清漳前鋒，其子尉遲安率騎兵出遼口向高句麗求援，死於半路。
peopleEn: Yuwen Jiong was an old general of Yuwen Tai, one of the Eight Pillars of Western Wei, who had served both Emperor Wu and Emperor Xuan of Zhou and reached the offices of chancellor and grand preceptor; he was the only heavyweight of the late Zhou able to hold down the consort clans and the army. He had worked the Hebei region for generations, the old families of Zhao and Wei commanderies and the Zhou imperial guard all acknowledged his banner, and the defences and grain stores of the Ye area were in his hands. Yang Jian was the core of the Guanlong group, a grandson of Yuwen Tai whose father Yang Zhong had likewise been one of the Eight Pillars. After Emperor Xuan's death he combined the title Prince of Sui with the chancellorship and the general administration of all affairs, held the palace guard and the issue of rescripts, and in the first month of Kaihuang finally took the abdication of the Zhou emperor Gong. His chief reliance on the western front was the overseer Wang Yi of Taiyuan, a friend of Yang Jian since boyhood, who was made commander-in-chief of the expedition with the troops of five provinces, broke the vanguard at Qingzhang and pressed on towards Ye. Wei Jun, commander of Bingzhou, and Wei Yunqi, commander of Shanzhou, brought up cavalry and infantry, Wei Jun being defeated in the first action and falling back. On the Yellow River line alongside Wuzhi, Yu Zhongwen, commandant of Dong Commandery, met the enemy with a little over sixty horsemen and cut off some five hundred of them, and afterwards broke out and withdrew to the west. The name of the man who held Henei Commandery is not preserved in the surviving record; all that survives is that the county troops stood at Wuzhi behind the walls and waited for succour. On Yuwen Jiong's side, Liu Pijiang, Shi Daxia and Duan Ren led the vanguard at Qingzhang, while his son Yuwen An rode out through Liaokou with cavalry to seek help from Goguryeo and died on the road.
kits: 本役實際上陣的裝備來自北朝體系。步兵的基本兵器是長柄矛與槊，配刀戟，格鬥時以槊鋒直推或以戟援橫擊；槊有長短之別，首用鐵或銅，柄髹漆以標等級，軍中以漆記辨兵械的銳鈍。弓弩是主力火力：臂弓配箭供陣前射擊，蹶張弩與張力更大的弩機供守城與壓制，弩手披甲伏於塹壕之後或城堞之下，輪番齊射以消耗敵軍陣形。護具方面，北周將士戴兜鍪，鍪頂以冡連護住後頸，另有肩甲、胸甲、臂韝與護腿，騎兵配頸護與馬具；作戰靠面旗、鼓與角傳令，軍令抵達的速度往往比刀槊的耐用度更要緊。馬匹來自涼州、並州與河北牧場，騎兵多配馬鎧與長槊，疾馳衝陣與追擊潰兵是尉遲迥軍的主要戰法。攻城與後勤器械有壘柵、壕溝、撞車、雲梯、投石機與砲石，糧食用牛車與黃河漕船分運。卡面的斯巴達長矛出自公元前八世紀的希臘：兩米長的木槍，槍尾套銅以便插地支撐，槍頭為葉形鐵刃——它並未出現在這場戰役，中國的出土器物與文獻中沒有同型實物；並排看則可看清兩套兵制的分歧，希臘人靠矛牆的正面厚度定勝負，北周的步卒同樣以長槊結陣前推，卻更依賴隊形紀律、旗鼓與弓弩。
kitsEn: The equipment actually in the line came from the northern Chinese armoured tradition. The basic infantry arm was the long-shafted spear and the long spear, with sabre and halberd alongside; in close fighting the long spear was pushed straight forward and the halberd swung as a hooking and cutting arm. Long spears came in more than one length, with iron or bronze heads, and the shaft was lacquered to mark grade, the lacquer being how an army told good serviceable arms from worn ones. Bow and crossbow provided the main volume of fire: the arm bow and its arrows for shooting in the open, the strong-drawn crossbow and the larger tension engines for holding a wall or crushing a formation, the crossbowmen armoured and lying behind ditch or parapet, firing in turns to grind down the enemy order. For protection, Zhou troops wore the domed helmet whose crown was guarded at the nape by a lamellar neck guard, with shoulder, breast, arm and thigh pieces besides, and cavalry had a neck guard and harness; orders were passed by face flags, drums and horns, and the speed at which an order travelled mattered more than the durability of any blade. Horses came from the pastures of Liangzhou, Bingzhou and Hebei, and the cavalry went into action in mail with the long spear, charging at speed and riding down broken men being the main method of Yuwen Jiong's army. The siege and baggage train included stockades, ditches, battering rams, scaling ladders, traction engines and stone shot, while grain moved in ox carts and in boats on the Yellow River. The dory on this card comes from eighth-century Greece: a two-metre shaft of wood, with a bronze butt-spike so that it could be planted in the ground, and a leaf-shaped iron head. It did not appear in this campaign; no matching object has been found in Chinese finds or Chinese texts. Set the two side by side, though, and the divergence of two systems becomes clear: the Greeks decided a battle with the frontal thickness of their spear wall, while Zhou infantry also advanced in ordered ranks with long spears, but leaned far more on discipline, on flags and drums, and on bow and crossbow.
tactics: 楊堅一方的打法是先斷政治外援，再動兵。宣帝崩後，他以中樞名義宣布尉遲迥不奉遺詔，令天下州郡兵入京，使河北與關東的郡縣不敢接應，隨後才分兵討伐。西線的部署是守住洛陽、據住黃河津渡，使河北來的敵軍不能直接進窺關中：河內郡的郡兵據縣城與渡口拒守，關隴騎兵在黃河灘地與城郊的野地反擊來敵，步卒以弩陣封住接近的道路，待敵鋒受挫、隊形散亂再以長槊壓上。韋俊的騎兵首戰失利後，楊堅改以王誼為大都督，統五州兵作步騎混合的戰鬥，以弩騎與步卒混編先破前鋒，再進逼鄴城。攻城階段，隋軍築壘挖壕、填平外壕，架攻城具，以弩箭與砲石覆射城頭，再以撞車與雲梯貼近城牆；同時分兵斷糧道、絕援兵、掃清鄴、鄒、曹各處的響應據點。尉遲迥以守代攻，重兵守鄴城拒敵，派前鋒在城南清漳一線迎隋軍，用前鋒的崩潰拖延隋軍接近城垣，並遣騎兵出遼口求援。黃河沿線的郵驛與漕船節節傳遞命令，兩翼的郡兵與援軍在武陟一線接應，構成此役的補給與指揮骨架。
tacticsEn: Yang Jian's method was to cut off political support first and only then to move troops. After Emperor Xuan's death he declared from the central court that Yuwen Jiong had not accepted the late emperor's instructions, and ordered the provincial levies of the whole realm into the capital, so that the commanderies of Hebei and the eastern districts would not dare to answer Yuwen Jiong's call; the campaigning came afterwards. On the western front the object was to hold Luoyang and to keep the fords of the Yellow River, so that an army coming out of Hebei could not slip into Guanzhong behind the capital's back. The county troops of Henei held the walled town and the crossings, the Guanlong cavalry answered the enemy in the open ground of the river flats and the fields outside the walls, and the infantry sealed the approaches with ranks of crossbowmen, waiting for the enemy charge to be checked and its order to come apart before pressing forward with the long spear. After Wei Jun's cavalry was beaten in the first action, Yang Jian changed the command to Wang Yi as grand overseer with the troops of five provinces, fighting with infantry and cavalry mixed together, breaking the vanguard with crossbows and horse, and only then closing on Ye. In the siege the Sui troops raised stockades, dug ditches, filled in the outer defences, brought up their engines, covered the walls with arrow and stone, and then closed in with rams and ladders; at the same time they cut the supply roads, severed succour, and reduced the points of revolt at Ye, Zou and Cao. Yuwen Jiong chose to defend rather than to attack: he kept the mass of his troops within Ye, sent the vanguard out to meet the Sui army on the Qingzhang south of the city in the hope that a broken vanguard would slow them short of the walls, and rode out with cavalry through Liaokou to seek foreign help. The postal relay and the river boats along the Yellow River carried the orders stage by stage, and the provincial troops and relief columns on both flanks linked up on the Wuzhi line; that was the framework of command and supply on which this engagement rested.
data: 可核對的數字大致落在同一個量級上。尉遲迥起兵時眾號十餘萬，通鑑記其起兵後郡縣響應者眾，兵眾在鄴城與周邊州縣集結，多屬河北鄉兵與北周宿衛舊部，戰力參差。楊堅方面第一波是韋俊的騎兵，兵力當在數千至一萬之間，敗後改以王誼統「五州兵」，依《隋書》王誼傳所載未逐一列出州名，人數當在數萬。清漳一役斬首萬餘級，是本役唯一有明確斬獲紀錄的野戰數字；尉遲安出遼口求援的騎兵記為五千；鄴城破後追隨尉遲迥的眾二十餘萬一朝散盡。時間上，自大象二年秋起兵到同年冬城破，前後約三個月；楊堅受禪的開皇元年正月已在平亂之後。距離上，洛陽至武陟直線不足八十公里，道路約一百一十公里；武陟至鄴城直線約一百四十公里，沿太行陘道約一百八十公里；黃河水路自武陟東至白馬津約九十公里。關於武陟一役本身，現存記載只留下交戰方向與結果，雙方投入兵力、斬獲數與死傷數皆無明確記載；按同期同一戰爭其他戰線的規模推估，此役投入當在數千至數萬之間，但這是推算而非史書所記。
dataEn: The verifiable figures cluster at the same order of magnitude. When Yuwen Jiong rose he claimed more than a hundred thousand men, and the Tongjian records that commanderies and counties answered in numbers, the troops massing at Ye and in the prefectures around it, for the most part Hebei village levies and former Zhou guard soldiers of uneven quality. The first wave on Yang Jian's side was Wei Jun's cavalry, on the order of several thousand to ten thousand; after that defeat Yang Jian set Wang Yi over the 'troops of five provinces', a phrase taken from Wang Yi's biography in the History of Sui which does not list the provinces, so the number was probably in the tens of thousands. The action at Qingzhang, which cut off more than ten thousand heads, is the only field engagement of the whole war with an explicit record of takings; the cavalry Yuwen An sent out through Liaokou in search of help is put at five thousand; and the more than two hundred thousand men who had followed Yuwen Jiong dispersed in a single night once Ye fell. In time, from the rising in the autumn of the Daxiang era to the fall of Ye in the same winter, the campaign ran about three months, and the first month of Kaihuang in which Yang Jian received the abdication came after the trouble was settled. In distance, Luoyang lies under eighty kilometres from Wuzhi in a straight line, roughly a hundred and ten by road; Wuzhi is about a hundred and forty kilometres from Ye in a straight line, a hundred and eighty by the Taihang road; and by the Yellow River it is about ninety kilometres from Wuzhi to Baima Ford. As for the action at Wuzhi itself, the surviving record preserves only the direction of the fighting and its result: the numbers committed on either side, the tally of the enemy slain and the casualty returns are all missing. Judging by the scale of the other fronts of the same war, the force engaged here was probably in the thousands or the tens of thousands, but that is an estimate and not a figure written down in the histories.
cause: 大象二年春，宣帝宇文贊病危，遺下年幼的宇文閔，朝廷隨即分成兩組人：以隨王楊堅為相國、總百揆、掌禁軍宿衛的關隴執政集團，和以丞相尉遲迥為首、握北周實際軍權與河北地盤的軍功舊臣。楊堅在先帝末年已進爵隨王、加相國，宿衛與詔令漸歸其手，尉遲迥身為大冢宰卻被一步步架空到只剩虛名，兩人的矛盾由權位之爭變成生死之爭。直接導火線是楊堅對北方軍權的整頓：詔令天下州郡兵入京、遣使巡察河北、收攏大將部曲與宿衛，這些動作在關隴集團看來是收編，在河北看來是逼反。尉遲迥遂在秋日於鄴城舉兵，遣使遊說州郡，以匡扶王室、誅姦黨為名，河北與山東郡縣多數響應，並與同時在並州起兵的太原王謙南北互為犄角。外因也不是偶然：北周連年伐陳，梁郡、利州等戰役耗去大批丁役與糧秣，關中與河北同時吃緊，北面還有突厥窺伺，尉遲迥指望的正是楊堅顧此失彼的窗口。河北世族素來輕視關隴新貴，擔心世代產業與部曲被中央收回，於是擁護聲浪極高。開戰的地點選在武陟，也是這個道理：握有太行孔道與黃河津渡的一側，才談得上把洛陽與河北分開。
causeEn: In the spring of the second year of Daxiang, Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun lay dying and left behind the child Yuwen Min, and the court split at once into two parties: the Guanlong governing group, with Yang Jian as Prince of Sui, chancellor and general administrator of all affairs, holding the palace guard, and the old military men of the court, headed by Chancellor Yuwen Jiong, who held Northern Zhou's real military power and its Hebei base. Yang Jian had already been raised to Prince of Sui and made chancellor late in the previous reign, and the guard and the rescripts had drifted his way, while Yuwen Jiong, grand preceptor as he was, was hollowed out until nothing remained but an empty title; the quarrel between the two men turned from a contest of rank into a contest for life. The immediate occasion was Yang Jian's overhaul of the military power of the north: the order bringing the provincial levies of the whole realm into the capital, the sending out of envoys to inspect Hebei, the gathering in of the generals' troops and of the guard. To the Guanlong group this looked like a rounding-up of the army; to Hebei it looked like a forced revolt. Yuwen Jiong accordingly raised his banner at Ye in the autumn, sent envoys to sound out the commanderies, and took for his watchword the restoration of the royal house and the chastisement of the evil ministers, and the commanderies of Hebei and of western Shandong answered in great number, while at the same time the prince of Taiyuan, Wang Qian, rose in Bingzhou to make a second front to the north and the south. The occasion was not accidental either: Northern Zhou had been campaigning against Chen year after year, the wars of Liang Commandery and of Lizhou consuming great numbers of levies and of grain, so that Guanzhong and Hebei were both short of resources, while in the north the Turks were pressing; what Yuwen Jiong counted on was a moment when Yang Jian could not attend to everything at once. The Hebei clans had long looked down on the newer families of Guanlong and feared that the holdings and the retainers of their generations would be taken back by the centre, and the clamour for him was accordingly loud. That the fighting should be joined at Wuzhi followed the same reasoning: only the side that held the road through the Taihang range and the fords of the Yellow River could talk of separating Luoyang from Hebei.
impact: 武陟與東郡白馬津這一線沒有失守，對全局的意義遠大於戰場本身：只要洛陽—太行陘道與黃河漕運保持暢通，楊堅的關中宿衛就不必東調，河北來的敵軍無法切斷糧道，也無法直接威脅洛陽與關中。尉遲迥的西進一旦在武陟受阻，河北的兵只能退回鄴城，最後被合圍；反過來說，若武陟先失，北周的存亡就會在幾日之內見分曉。戰後，河北與山東的世族武裝被解除武柄，郡兵、鄉兵與北周宿衛舊部大量被收編入隋軍，成為隋禁軍與河北防務的骨幹；關隴八柱國的部曲升格為國家軍隊的核心，兩種兵源合流。制度上，楊堅在戰時下詔「天下州郡兵入京」，開了隋唐前期把地方兵權收歸中央的先例。開皇元年正月楊堅受周恭帝禪讓，國號隋，改元開皇；開皇八年冬隋軍渡江滅陳，統一南北。對外關係上，高句麗沒有接納尉遲安的反叛，突厥仍在北方游弋，北疆隱患並未解除。
impactEn: That the line of Wuzhi and Baima Ford was not lost mattered far more to the war than the field itself. So long as the road from Luoyang through the Taihang passes and the grain traffic on the Yellow River stayed open, Yang Jian's Guanlong guard never had to march east, the army out of Hebei could neither cut the supply line nor come directly at Luoyang or Guanzhong. Once Yuwen Jiong's westward movement was checked at Wuzhi, the Hebei troops could only fall back on Ye and were finally shut up there; put the other way, had Wuzhi fallen first, the survival of Northern Zhou would have been decided within a few days. After the war, the armed bands of the Hebei and Shandong clans were stripped of their weapons, and large numbers of county levies, village levies and former Zhou guard troops were taken into the Sui armies, where they became the backbone of the Sui palace guard and of the northern defences; the troops of the Eight Pillars of Guanlong were raised to the status of the core of the national army, and the two sources of men were fused. In institutional terms, the order Yang Jian issued during the war that the provincial levies of the whole realm should come into the capital set the precedent for bringing local military power under central control in the early Sui and Tang. In the first month of Kaihuang Yang Jian took the abdication of the Zhou emperor Gong, the state was renamed Sui and the era renamed Kaihuang; in the winter of the eighth year of Kaihuang the Sui armies crossed the river and destroyed Chen, uniting north and south. In foreign affairs, Goguryeo did not take in the rebel Yuwen An, and the Turks continued to prowl the northern frontier, so that the danger along the northern border was not removed.
result: 大象二年冬，鄴城在隋軍合圍與斷糧之後陷落，尉遲迥自刎於軍中，諸子皆死，追隨他的眾二十餘萬一朝星散，多數解散還鄉，一部分被隋軍收編。河北與山東的響應點隨之瓦解：劉辟疆據鄒城兵敗被殺，兗州刺史高寶慶與曹州刺史邵公明的武裝被逐一打掉，齊州刺史尉遲熾為司州刺史拓跋儁所擒斬，尉遲氏在北周的舊勢力至此根除。就武陟一線而言，結果是尉遲迥西進的企圖徹底落空：守方保住了縣城與津渡，敵軍退回東岸，河北的兵源與糧源無法與關中接觸，北周得以在無內亂牽制的條件下完成交接。楊堅這邊付出的代價也記在史書裡：王誼薨於軍中，韋俊的騎兵初戰失利，說明關隴兵在河北並非所向無敵；若不是韋孝寬在東線與王誼在鄴城穩住陣腳，收拾殘局拖成另一場消耗戰，尉遲迥未必會在同年冬天崩潰。開皇年間對河北的編戶與州兵整頓，源頭正起於這場平叛之後的收拾殘局。
resultEn: In the winter of the second year of Daxiang, after the Sui army had closed in and cut off the grain, Ye fell; Yuwen Jiong cut his own throat in the camp, all his sons died with him, and the more than two hundred thousand men who had followed him scattered in a single night, most going home, some taken over into the Sui ranks. The points of revolt in Hebei and Shandong were then picked off one by one: Liu Pijiang, who had held Zou city, was defeated and killed; the armed followers of the Yan prefecture's governor Gao Baoqing and of the Cao prefecture's governor Shao Gongming were destroyed in turn; the governor of Qi prefecture, Yuwen Chi, was taken and beheaded by Tuoba Jun, governor of Si prefecture; and with that the old power of the Yuwen clan in Northern Zhou was rooted out. On the Wuzhi line the result was that Yuwen Jiong's attempt to march west failed completely: the defenders kept the walled town and the crossings, the enemy withdrew to the eastern bank, and the men and the grain of Hebei could not come within reach of Guanzhong, so that Northern Zhou was able to complete the transfer of power with no rebellion tying it down. The price Yang Jian paid is also written down in the histories: Wang Yi died in the camp, and Wei Jun's cavalry was beaten in the first action, which shows that the troops of Guanlong were not invincible in Hebei. Had Wei Xiaokuan on the eastern front and Wang Yi before Ye not held the line, and had the business of mopping up been drawn out into a war of attrition of another kind, Yuwen Jiong would not necessarily have collapsed in that same winter. The registering of households and the reform of the county levies in Hebei in the Kaihuang years began in the clean-up that followed this suppression.
